clue.text: Applaud role, but on reflection, it's regarded as nonsense

parts.note: to applaud is to clap

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the word for role is read backwards

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: Someone praises an acting role, then thinks better of it and calls it rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns PART into TRAP; 'it's regarded as' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious empty talk, a synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Take catch, and win

definitions.meaning: to bring a fish to shore
to secure something, as a contract

explanation.definitionFit: An angler lands a fish, and a firm lands a deal it has won.

clue.text: One may turn up in quiet lake on island

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
lough is the Irish word for a lake
the Isle of Man, often just Man

explanation.surface: Someone appears on an Irish lake on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'on' are links; 'turn up' means turn up soil, not arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploughman turns up the soil with a plough.

clue.text: What may be left by, one departing this life?

definitions.text: What may be left by, one departing this life?

indicators.note: departing means leaving, so the letter for one goes out of the word

parts.note: this life, the real world, is reality
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question about what a dying person leaves behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Realty is real estate, property often left in a will.

clue.text: Epistle, torn open, seen to be crudely written

definitions.text: Epistle, torn open, seen to be crudely written

indicators.note: something crudely written is scrawled, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A letter ripped open turns out to be scrawled crudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen to be' links; the whole clue also describes the answer, a nasty letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison-pen letter is an anonymous malicious epistle, often crudely written.

clue.text: Principal drinking port had one over the eight? Not quite that many!

definitions.text: one over the eight? Not quite that many!

indicators.note: something drinking takes another thing into itself, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a principal of a school or college is its head
Pt is the abbreviation for port on maps and in place names

explanation.surface: A head teacher drinks port and ends up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for being drunk; read literally it is nine, and 'not quite that many' takes it down to seven.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptad is a group of seven, one short of eight and so not quite 'one over the eight'.

clue.text: Hot temper' over freeloader?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
temper here means anger
on means about or concerning, as over does

explanation.surface: A host loses their temper with a sponger.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a sycophantic follower who sponges, a freeloader.

clue.text: After turning tap on check temporary repair

indicators.note: turning tells us the word tap is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ch is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A plumber turns a tap and checks a quick fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' and 'on' are links placing the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a makeshift repair.

clue.text: They won't be drinking, .and shuffling about seats in bar

indicators.note: shuffling moves things round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teetotallers move around the seats in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstainers are teetotallers, people who refuse alcohol.

clue.text: What's new in pub getting great reception?

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is a rapturous reception from an audience

explanation.surface: Someone asks what novelty a pub has to earn such applause.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is a novelty, something newly introduced.

clue.text: Objection — not in favour of type of examination

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letters meaning in favour

parts.note: a protest is an objection
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone objects that they dislike a certain kind of exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is a kind of examination, as in a driving test.

clue.text: Make drunk visit the boss?

definitions.meaning: alcohol that intoxicates someone is said to do this
read literally, going to see the person in charge of you

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to intoxicate; read literally it means calling on your head of department.

clue.text: Getting ready, after initial lapse, to make redress

indicators.note: the first letter lapses, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: getting ready is preparation

explanation.surface: Someone prepares to make amends after an initial slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparation is compensation for a wrong, redress.

clue.text: Smile, given support

definitions.meaning: a horizontal timber or girder holding up a structure

explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to smile radiantly, and a beam is a structural support.

clue.text: Make a submission, showing disapproval of the euro?

definitions.meaning: to put forward an idea for consideration
read as ..., favouring the British currency over the euro

explanation.surface: A Eurosceptic presents a case against the single currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound is to put forward a proposal; split as pro-pound it means backing sterling.

clue.text: People of Europe or people of North America? Not North America

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Not tells us to leave out those letters

parts.note: Canadians are people of North America

explanation.surface: A quiz question about which continent some people belong to.
explanation.walkthrough: Orcadians are Orkney islanders, in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcadians, natives of Orkney, are a European people.

clue.text: Fare not including waiter service?

parts.note: food you buy over a counter quickly, with no one serving at the table

explanation.definitionFit: Fast food is quickly served takeaway fare without table service.

clue.text: Claim support

definitions.meaning: to keep something up or provide for it

explanation.definitionFit: To maintain is both to assert a claim and to keep something supported.

clue.text: Snappy cricket stroke picking up runs

indicators.note: picking up means taking something in, so one letter goes inside the stroke

parts.note: a cut is a cricket stroke played square on the off side
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sharp cricket shot scores runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt means brusque, snappy in manner.

clue.text: Face revealed how old woman is

parts.note: Vi is a woman's name
's is short for is
age is how old someone is

explanation.surface: A face gives away a woman's age.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as VI'S AGE: the age of Vi; 'revealed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary word for face.

clue.text: Get the necessary rain, with seed broadcast

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer sows seed by scattering and hopes for rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The necessary' is slang for money; 'raise the wind' is an old British idiom for getting hold of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise the wind is an idiom for obtaining needed money, the necessary.

clue.text: Old novel and SF film advertised in newspaper

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's 1887 novel
ET is Spielberg's science-fiction film

explanation.surface: A classic novel and a sci-fi film are promoted in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advertised in' is a link; a sheet is slang for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheet is informal for a newspaper, as in a scandal sheet.

clue.text: Nymph's given ring

definitions.meaning: the mountain nymph in Greek myth who could only repeat others' words

explanation.definitionFit: Echo was a Greek nymph, and to echo is to ring out again.

clue.text: A drink that'll give you bellyache, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word said out loud sounds like the answer

parts.note: to bellyache is to whine or complain

explanation.surface: A warning about a drink that will upset your stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Count, more importantly, worried about sharp weapon used

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters of about are shaken into a new order

parts.note: a lance is a pointed weapon

explanation.surface: A nobleman is anxious about a sharp weapon being used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns ABOUT into OUTBA; 'used' is a link. 'Count' looks like a nobleman but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbalance is to outweigh, to count for more than something else.

clue.text: Got together, or the opposite if it's over

indicators.note: the letters IT are turned over within the word for the opposite

parts.note: the opposite of joined together is untied

explanation.surface: A riddle about joining up, or splitting, depending on circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: UNTIED contains TI; turning those two letters 'over' to IT gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: United means joined together.

clue.text: A lot of grass — drug put back in pipes

parts.note: reeds are tall grasses, and the plural gives a lot of them

indicators.note: put back tells us the drug word is written in reverse

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Grass and drugs are stuffed back into smoking pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns POT into TOP; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed stop is an organ stop controlling a rank of reed pipes.
